newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says early Telekom sale possible.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says early Telekom sale possible.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Wednesday that an early sale of the government's remaining 75 percent stake in Deutsche Telekom AG was possible.
"It is conceivable that parts of the privatisation of Telekom could be brought forward," Waigel told journalists in Bonn.
Waigel says early Telekom sale possible

Waigel told reporters that he did not expect the government sale would negatively affect either Telekom or around two million private shareholders who participated in the company's landmark initial public offering last November.
"With the company's exquisite state of health a sale of shares would not be a problem," Waigel said.
"We have more than 70 percent in Telekom and we don't need that much. A company and its share price that have blossomed and flourished like Telekom does not need the government," he added.
While German law does not explicitly rule out the government selling its shares before the year 2000, it has been widely believed that this would only be possible under extraordinary circumstances.

Telekom Chairman Ron Sommer told the daily Bild newspaper in a report to appear on Thursday that German law requires the government to seek approval from the Telekom management board for a sale of shares that would impact the market before December 31, 1999.

"Such a measure requires the approval of the management board," said Sommer. "We will ensure that the interests of the nearly two million shareholders are not affected. There is complete agreement on this point between the finance minister and myself," he said.
